f: Largest city in Central America, set in a highland valley ringed by volcanoes such as Pacaya.
Island town on Lake Petén Itzá and the gateway to the Maya ruins of Tikal.
Belize is the only Central American country where English is the official language.
Honduras' industrial and commercial capital in all but name.
Toncontin airport has a steep approach between mountains, among the most demanding in the world.
Largest of the Bay Islands, beside the Mesoamerican Barrier Reef.
El Salvador uses the US dollar and made bitcoin legal tender in 2021.
A 1972 earthquake destroyed much of the city center.
Costa Rica abolished its army in 1948.
Its airport serves Guanacaste's Pacific beaches, a major ecotourism region.
Home hub of Copa Airlines, connecting most of Latin America; the Canal opened in 1914.
Caribbean entrance of the Panama Canal, with one of the world's largest free trade zones.
Caribbean archipelago in Panama popular for snorkeling and surfing.
At about 2,600 m, one of the highest capital cities in the world.
Its Metrocable gondolas link hillside neighborhoods to the metro.
Widely called the salsa capital of the world.
Its walled colonial city is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
Colombian island that lies far closer to Nicaragua than to the Colombian mainland.
Sits in a valley separated from the Caribbean coast by the Ávila mountain.
Oil city on Lake Maracaibo, near the Catatumbo lightning phenomenon.
Gateway to Angel Falls, the world's tallest uninterrupted waterfall at 979 m.

Savanna border town with Brazil, linked across the Takutu River by a bridge.

Part of France and the EU, and home to Europe's spaceport at Kourou.

Ecuador's largest city and main port.
Home of the Charles Darwin Research Station in the Galápagos.
One of the driest capital cities in the world, with almost no rain.
Former Inca capital and gateway to Machu Picchu, at about 3,400 m.
Largest city in the Peruvian Amazon, with no road link to the rest of Peru; reached only by air or river.

Bolivia's largest city and its main economic engine.
Gateway to the Salar de Uyuni, the world's largest salt flat.
Constitutional capital of Bolivia, while the government sits in La Paz.
Largest city in the Southern Hemisphere and home to the B3 stock exchange.
Christ the Redeemer was completed in 1931.
Planned capital inaugurated in 1960, designed by Lúcio Costa and Oscar Niemeyer.
Where the Rio Negro meets the Solimões; its opera house dates from the 1896 rubber boom.
Gateway to the Amazon delta; it hosted the COP30 climate summit in 2025.
First capital of colonial Brazil.
Built across rivers and islands, it is often called the Venice of Brazil.
Brazil's closest big city to Europe and North America, a hub for subsea cables.
Capital of Rio Grande do Sul, the home of gaúcho culture.
Pioneered bus rapid transit in the 1970s.
Planned capital of Minas Gerais, founded in 1897.
Volcanic archipelago about 350 km off Brazil, a UNESCO site with a strict visitor cap.
Next to Iguazu Falls, shared with Argentina, and the Itaipu dam.
One of the oldest cities in South America, founded in 1537.
Tri-border trade hub with Brazil and Argentina, near the Itaipu dam.
Gran Torre Santiago, at 300 m, is the tallest building in South America.
Port and service hub for the copper mines of the Atacama Desert.
Serves Chuquicamata, one of the world's largest open-pit copper mines.
Hosts Zofri, a duty-free trade zone in the Atacama desert.
Largest city in the far south of the continent, on the Strait of Magellan.
Often called the southernmost town in the world.
Easter Island's moai statues stand about 2,000 km from the nearest inhabited land, Pitcairn.
On Robinson Crusoe Island, where Alexander Selkirk was marooned, inspiring Defoe's novel.
Birthplace of tango, together with Montevideo.
Home to the oldest university in Argentina, founded in 1613.
Heart of Argentina's wine country and its Malbec production.
Hub of the soy-crushing ports on the Paraná river.
Commonly called the southernmost city in the world and a departure point for Antarctica.
Alpine lake resort in Patagonia.
Gateway to the Perito Moreno Glacier.
More than half of Uruguay's people live in the capital area.
Resort peninsula famed for the La Mano sculpture on Playa Brava.

Explorer Ernest Shackleton is buried in the old whalers' cemetery here.
Napoleon died in exile on Saint Helena in 1821.

Most remote inhabited island, about 2,400 km from Saint Helena; reached only by ship from Cape Town (about 6 days).
Largest research station in Antarctica, home to about 1,200 people in summer and 150 to 200 in winter.
Sits at the geographic South Pole on ice about 2,835 m above sea level.
British Antarctic Survey's main station, with a gravel runway on Adelaide Island.
Argentine base on Seymour Island with a gravel runway used by C-130 Hercules.
Private camp with a blue-ice runway, used for expeditions to the South Pole and Mount Vinson.
Norway's year-round station in Queen Maud Land, about 235 km inland.

Argentine base where Emilio Palma became the first person born on the continent, in 1978.
Chilean settlement on King George Island with a school, bank and post office.
Franco-Italian Dome C base at 3,233 m, where small winter crews are cut off for months.
